name: Rook
greeting: You got the cart moving? Good. I was about to sell him a very expensive push.
lines: Rook: Bram fixed my axle twice. Charged me once. Claimed he could not afford to be seen with a grateful smuggler.
Kael: You knew the other two?
Rook: Sella asked about the old road. Oren asked whether the crows paid me to follow them.
Rook: The road bends where the old waystone says it should not. I have a map. I also have a room somebody can find.

actions.label: Copy the route. Keep the families' homes private.
actions.result: Rook marks a usable road without family addresses. He agrees to speak to the route under protection.
actions.preview: Rook marks a usable road without family addresses. He agrees to speak to the route under protection.
actions.cost: A public route can endanger marked families; a destroyed map cannot help the next traveler.

actions.label: Destroy the map. Keep the route between us.
actions.result: The paper burns. The road remains in Rook's memory, but no stranger can follow a copy now.
actions.preview: The paper burns. The road remains in Rook's memory, but no stranger can follow a copy now.
actions.cost: A public route can endanger marked families; a destroyed map cannot help the next traveler.

actions.label: Publish the marked map so everyone can challenge Vargan.
actions.result: The route becomes public evidence. Rook takes his bedding from the window; he did not consent to exposing his family.
actions.preview: The route becomes public evidence. Rook takes his bedding from the window; he did not consent to exposing his family.
actions.cost: A public route can endanger marked families; a destroyed map cannot help the next traveler.

variants.greeting: They copied the map with my family mark still on it. A guard came to my door.
lines: Rook: You needed a witness. You got a target as well.
Kael: I will keep a way out open.
Rook: That was meant to be the promise before you put my name up.

variants.greeting: I copied the route without the houses. The families know who has the original.
lines: Rook: I will tell the assembly what I saw. They do not need my grandmother's bedroom to believe it.
Kael: You choose what is yours to share.
Rook: There. A sentence I could get used to.

variants.greeting: I can still walk the route. I will not make another map for you.
lines: Rook: Destroying the copy kept Vargan from using it. It kept the next refugee from using it too.
Kael: I can carry the route in the record without your family mark.

variants.greeting: The guard asked where my grandmother lived. Said he was checking who deserved protection.
lines: Rook: My family kept names because the shrine would not. That does not make us willing to be nailed to a board.
Kael: I promised to stay with the people carrying this.
Rook: Then stay where they can reach you. The false waystone is a good start.
